sections.title: Front matter

summary.text: The front matter of WHO policy guidance on using loop-mediated isothermal amplification (TB-LAMP) to diagnose pulmonary tuberculosis. It includes the cover, cataloguing data with ISBN, copyright and disclaimer notices, and a table of contents covering methods, results of the systematic review, cost-effectiveness and recommendations. It also contains acknowledgements and lists of contributors. It ends with the declarations of interest of Guideline Development Group members and the planned review date of 2020.

sections.title: Executive summary

summary.text: Summarizes the TB-LAMP policy guidance, explaining the End TB Strategy's call for early diagnosis and how the manual LAMP assay works and can be read under ultraviolet light. It recounts the 2012 Guideline Development Group review and the newer evidence assessment. It then states the conditional recommendations for using TB-LAMP instead of, or after, sputum-smear microscopy, together with remarks limiting their scope.

sections.title: Background

summary.text: Sets out the background to TB-LAMP, noting that a large share of TB cases worldwide go undetected and that new diagnostics are a priority. It describes the commercial Eiken assay, its modest infrastructure needs and its history of WHO review. It then walks through the TB-LAMP workflow, from sample preparation and heating to visual reading of fluorescence and waste disposal.

sections.extract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a large-scale public health problem. Key global priorities for TB care and control include improving case-detection and detecting patients earlier, particularly patients with smear-negative TB disease. sections.title: Evidence synthesis

summary.text: Explains that the GRADE approach and PICO-framed questions were used to assess the evidence on TB-LAMP. It lists the four review questions on accuracy versus microscopy, use as an add-on test, comparison with Xpert MTB/RIF, and rates of invalid results.

sections.extract: In accordance with WHO’s standards for assessing evidence when formulating policy recommendations, the GRADE approach (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation, see http://www.gradeworkinggroup.org/) was used. sections.title: Criteria for considering studies for this review

summary.text: Defines which TB-LAMP studies were eligible for the systematic review, including prospective studies after 2012 in intermediate- and high-burden settings and a supplementary literature search. It lists exclusion criteria for studies and individual participants and describes the culture-based reference standards and smear microscopy definitions used.

sections.extract: The review included all prospective studies that evaluated the use of TB-LAMP on sputum samples from adults with signs and symptoms consistent with pulmonary TB that were conducted in settings with an intermediate or high burden of TB. All included studies were conducted after 1 January 2012, using the final, design-locked TB-LAMP protocol that had been modified by the manufacturer. Twenty studies were identified,

sections.title: Data collection and analysis

summary.text: Describes how individual-level data were obtained from FIND-affiliated and other TB-LAMP studies, listing the minimum and optional variables collected. It then outlines how accuracy, incremental yield and invalid result rates were calculated and how heterogeneity was assessed.

sections.extract: For studies conducted by or funded through FIND, study protocols, inclusion criteria and definitions were provided by FIND along with data on individual participants. Further review of the individual- level data was performed to verify that the study and individual participants met eligibility criteria. sections.title: Guideline Development Group meeting

summary.text: Notes that a WHO Guideline Development Group met in January 2016 to review 20 new TB-LAMP studies, 13 of which met inclusion criteria, and outlines the roles of the methodologist and Steering Group.

sections.extract: Following the initial GDG meeting on TB-LAMP in 2012, a GDG meeting was convened by WHO in January 2016 to review the evidence from 20 new studies, of which 13 studies conducted in 11 countries met the inclusion criteria. summary.text: Describes how the Steering Group handled interests, PICO questions and the consensus process for the TB-LAMP recommendations, and how an External Review Group of laboratory experts found no major errors or concerns in the guidance.

sections.title: Scope

summary.text: States that the guidance summarizes evidence and recommendations on using TB-LAMP for pulmonary TB in symptomatic adults and should be read with WHO's 2015 framework for implementing TB diagnostics.

sections.extract: 3. sections.title: Target audience

summary.text: Identifies the intended users of the TB-LAMP guidance, from clinicians and laboratory directors to donors, procurement officers and programme planners.

sections.extract: This guidance is intended to be used by clinicians treating patients with TB, and managers and laboratory directors working in TB programmes, in coordination with external laboratory consultants, donor agencies, technical advisers, laboratory technicians, procurement officers for laboratory equipment, service providers in the private sector, relevant government sectors, and implementation partners that are involved

sections.title: Evidence base for policy formulation

summary.text: Describes the evidence base for the TB-LAMP recommendations: of 20 studies identified, 13 in 11 countries met inclusion criteria, many of them unpublished. It explains the role of FIND in conducting or sponsoring most studies and gives participant numbers and study periods. Tables summarize study characteristics such as setting, HIV prevalence and reference standards.

sections.extract: Of the 20 studies identified that evaluated TB-LAMP, 13 studies conducted in 11 countries met the criteria for inclusion in the systematic review (Fig. 4). Six studies were excluded because it was unclear whether participants had been receiving TB treatment within 60 days prior to enrolment. sections.title: Assessment of methodological quality

summary.text: Reports the QUADAS-2 appraisal of the included TB-LAMP studies, judging overall risk of bias as high mainly because of the culture reference standard, unclear patient selection and flow and timing problems. A table gives each study's risk-of-bias and applicability ratings, and notes explain the judgements.

sections.extract: The quality of the included studies was appraised with the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies (QUADAS-2) tool.10 QUADAS-2 consists of four domains: patient selection, index test, reference standard, and flow and timing. sections.title: Accuracy of TB-LAMP as a replacement test for smear microscopy

summary.text: Presents the accuracy of TB-LAMP as a replacement for smear microscopy, with the numbers of eligible and included participants by study and reference standard. Forest plots and pooled sensitivity and specificity estimates are given for each of the three culture-based standards. Table notes define the standards used.

summary.text: Reports the limited data on TB-LAMP accuracy among adults living with HIV, giving the ranges of sensitivity and specificity across studies for each reference standard. It notes greater heterogeneity and provides pooled estimates in a table.

Pooled sensitivity and specificity for smear-negative, culture-positive TB are shown with forest plots. Table notes define the culture standards.

sections.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis

summary.text: Summarizes a costing study of TB-LAMP and Xpert MTB/RIF in peripheral laboratories in Malawi and Viet Nam, comparing TB-LAMP strategies with microscopy-based care. It gives per-test costs and affordability and cost-effectiveness findings, and cautions policy-makers to weigh feasibility and costs before adoption.

sections.title: Summary: from evidence to recommendations

summary.text: Introduces the evidence-to-recommendation summary, noting that TB-LAMP accuracy on sputum was determined from 13 studies in intermediate- and high-burden countries.

sections.extract: The accuracy of TB-LAMP performed directly on sputum samples for diagnosing pulmonary TB among adults who have not received TB treatment within 60 days of enrolment was determined from 13 studies performed in countries with intermediate and high burdens of TB.

sections.title: TB-LAMP for the detection of pulmonary TB in all adults

summary.text: Explains the Guideline Development Group's reasoning on TB-LAMP for all adults: higher sensitivity than microscopy with slightly lower specificity, partly attributed to culture misclassification. It weighs the extra cases detected per 1 000 tested against false positives and concludes the trade-off is acceptable.

sections.extract: Using data from the 1 810 persons with signs and symptoms consistent with TB for whom the most stringent reference standard could be used (Standard 1), TB-LAMP had a pooled sensitivity that was 15% higher than smear microscopy (78% compared with 63%). sections.title: TB-LAMP for the detection of pulmonary TB in adults living with HIV

summary.text: Reports that in a small HIV-positive group TB-LAMP performed about the same as smear microscopy, and explains why the group made no specific recommendation for people living with HIV, citing limited evidence.

sections.extract: Data from 4 studies (271 participants) that included HIV-positive adults with signs and symptoms consistent with pulmonary TB and that evaluated the accuracy of TB-LAMP demonstrated sensitivity and specificity similar to sputum-smear microscopy (sensitivity: 64% for TB-LAMP and 62% for smear microscopy; specificity: 99% for TB-LAMP and 99% for smear microscopy)(Annex 2, Table 11). sections.title: TB-LAMP as an add-on test for detecting of pulmonary TB in adults following negative smear microscopy

summary.text: Sets out the reasoning for TB-LAMP as an add-on test after negative smear microscopy, citing a 42% incremental yield and slightly lower specificity. It concludes that more cases would be found with an acceptable number of false positives.

sections.title: TB-LAMP as a replacement test for the Xpert MTB/RIF assay for detecting pulmonary TB in adults

summary.text: Compares TB-LAMP with Xpert MTB/RIF, noting lower sensitivity and no rifampicin resistance detection, and explains why Xpert remains preferred where resources allow while TB-LAMP may suit peripheral sites.

sections.extract: TB in adults Although better than microscopy, the pooled sensitivity of TB-LAMP is lower than what has been reported for the Xpert MTB/RIF assay (89%; 95% credible interval: 85–92).11 The specificity of all three tests is similar. sections.title: WHO policy recommendations

summary.text: States WHO's two conditional recommendations, based on very low-quality evidence, for TB-LAMP as a replacement for or follow-on to smear microscopy in symptomatic adults. Remarks restrict their use to sputum, caution against replacing rapid rifampicin-resistance tests and note uncertainty for people with HIV and extrapolation to children.

sections.title: Implementation considerations

summary.text: Lists implementation considerations for TB-LAMP, including electricity, storage temperature, waste disposal and stock needs. It also notes that smear microscopy is still needed for treatment monitoring and that Xpert MTB/RIF should not be replaced.

sections.extract: 9. Implementation considerations The systematic review supports the use of TB-LAMP as a replacement test for smear microscopy for diagnosing pulmonary TB in countries with an intermediate or high burden of TB. sections.title: Plans for disseminating WHO’s guidance on TB-LAMP

summary.text: Describes how the TB-LAMP guidance will be published online and distributed to WHO offices, Member States and partner networks.

sections.title: Research needs

summary.text: Lists research needs for TB-LAMP, such as studies with stronger culture reference standards, evaluation of diagnostic algorithms, training needs, patient impact and country-specific cost analyses.

sections.extract: 11. sections.title: GRADE Evidence Profiles

summary.text: Presents GRADE evidence profiles comparing TB-LAMP with sputum-smear microscopy for diagnosing pulmonary TB in adults, against a culture reference standard. Tables give pooled sensitivity and specificity and the expected true and false positives and negatives per 1000 patients at different pre-test probabilities. Footnotes explain why the evidence was rated very low or low quality, citing risk of bias, indirectness and heterogeneity across studies.

sections.title: Abstracts for unpublished studies

summary.text: Reproduces abstracts of unpublished studies on TB-LAMP included in the review, beginning with a Côte d'Ivoire study comparing smear microscopy, TB-LAMP and GeneXpert MTB/RIF against liquid culture in symptomatic patients. Each abstract outlines background, methods, sample sizes and the sensitivity and specificity results obtained. The section ends with WHO Global TB Programme contact details.
